situation.text: You are in a big supermarket in the United States. You cannot find the rice. You ask where it is, check if they have another kind and ask the price.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: American supermarkets are big. Look at the cards: what is different?

cards.note: Signs above the aisles list products: “Aisle 5 — Rice, Beans, Pasta.”
You scan and pay by yourself, but a worker helps if you need it.
In some places stores charge for bags, so many people bring their own.

qs.q: How do you find a product?

levels.A2: I read the signs or ask a worker.
levels.B1: I check the signs above the aisles or ask an employee.
levels.B2: I look at the aisle signs first, and if I can’t find it I ask a staff member.

levels.A2: You scan the food and pay at a machine.
levels.B1: You scan your items and pay without a cashier.
levels.B2: It’s a machine where you scan, bag and pay your own groceries.

qs.q: Why do people bring their own bag?
qs.pt: Por que levar a própria sacola?

levels.A2: In some places a bag costs money.
levels.B1: Some stores charge for bags, and it is better for the planet.
levels.B2: Some states and cities charge a fee or ban plastic bags, so reusable bags are common.

pages.compare: Many Brazilian supermarkets also have self-checkout and charge for bags. Where do you shop? Is it similar?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Every English word with more than one syllable has one strong syllable: ba-NA-na, to-MA-to, YO-gurt. A wrong stress can make a word hard to understand.

own.prompt: Choose a food word with 3 syllables from your shopping list. Mark the strong syllable.
own.criteria: Say it 3 times. Is the strong syllable louder and longer?

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: Excuse me. Where can I find rice?
Is there any brown rice? I can’t see it on the shelf.
I’m looking for a gluten-free pasta. Do you carry any?
I’d appreciate it if you could check whether another store has it in stock.
Might I trouble you to point me towards the best alternative?

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
